name: undercave_sky
description: Does a real Anomaly undercave track the sun? It is a sealed cave under the ground, so it should sit at the enclosed constant at every hour. The mod decides that through MapSky.IsEnclosed, which is derived from a weather-count heuristic, and Undercave's BiomeDef inherits from Biome_Underground so RimWorld's list merging gives it two weather entries -- over the threshold. Noon and midnight on one generated undercave, with the clock paused so each is a held moment. The assertion is that the two hours AGREE. Compare them WITHIN a run and never across runs: each run generates a fresh undercave, so two runs' frames differ in fleshmass layout as well as in lighting, and a cross-run frame diff measures the generator. Within a run the map is the same map. EnterPocketMap dirties ScenarioResidue.NewMap, so this runs standalone.

steps._comment: Paused so each hour below is a held moment rather than a moving one; see cloud_cover_skyless.json for what an unpaused clock does to a reading.
Throwaway: hideUi is not honoured on a run's first capture.
A real Anomaly undercave -- Anomaly's fleshy cavern under a monolith. Generated rather than painted, because the question is about a map kind and not a palette.

NOON. The whole question in one number: does a sealed cave under the ground track the sun?

A cave has no day, so the mod's enclosed-ambient patch is supposed to replace the diurnal curve with a constant here. It only fires when MapSky.IsEnclosed is true, and IsEnclosed is !hasSky && !inVacuum -- so a biome the weather-count heuristic calls skyful is not enclosed, and the sun comes back.

MIDNIGHT, same map, nothing else changed. If this differs from the noon reading the cave is tracking a sun it cannot see; if the two agree, the enclosed constant is in force.

MEASURED 0.0912 HERE BEFORE THE FIX, against 1.0000 at noon in the same run -- a sealed cave under a monolith going nearly black at midnight because the enclosed-ambient constant never engaged. Pinned TIGHT at both hours now: a cave has no day, so these two readings being the identical number is the assertion, not an approximation of one.

Warmth of the RENDERED overlay at midnight, as a second and independent witness.

It replaces a sky_color_temperature probe that was tried here first and rejected, which is worth recording because the mistake is easy to repeat: that probe recomputes the ramp from solar elevation and never consults MapSky.IsEnclosed, so it reads the same 2000 K whether or not Patch_SkyColorTemperature actually applied a tint. It is a FORMULA probe, and the question here is about APPLICATION. It read 2000 identically before and after the fix, which would have been mistaken for the fix not working.
